intent: Hold the chosen value, the typed query and the open state of one filterable field, and filter its list of items by what the user types.
typical_uses: One value picked from a long list that is faster to type into than to scroll
Several values picked from a list and shown as removable chips

dont_use_when.situation: One value from a short fixed list the user scrolls rather than searches
A short fixed list that should use the platform's own picker, such as on touch devices
A handful of options that should all stay visible at once
A searchable list of actions or commands to run, rather than a value to keep
Free text with no list to pick from

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

`inputValue` and `defaultInputValue` are both accepted; `defaultInputValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `inputValue` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.
`open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

Filtering runs over `items` and nothing else: with `items`, the root keeps the items whose label contains the typed query (a case- and accent-insensitive match unless `filter` replaces it), showing every item while a one-value field still holds the chosen item's label untouched since opening, and ComboboxList and ComboboxEmpty read that filtered result; without `items`, every statically rendered ComboboxItem stays visible whatever is typed and ComboboxEmpty shows its message at all times.

Without `multiple`, choosing an item makes it the value and closes the popup. With `multiple`, the value is an array: choosing an item adds it, choosing an already chosen item removes it, and the popup stays open unless a query had been typed.

Once the popup has finished closing, a one-value field's text is set back to the chosen item's label, or emptied when nothing is chosen, and a multiple-value field's typed query is emptied; typed text never becomes the value by itself.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave out `items` and render the ComboboxItem elements by hand
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass the full list as `items` and render ComboboxList's children as a function of each item, so typing filters the list and ComboboxEmpty shows only when nothing matches

anti_patterns.dont: Use a combobox to navigate between pages
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use links, or the app router's own navigation; a combobox holds a value, and choosing an item only changes that value

children.states: children is the root's content, React nodes holding the field and the popup
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

value.states: value is the chosen item, or an array of chosen items with `multiple`, or null for no choice
value.because: `ComboboxValueType<Value, Multiple> | null` - `Value` is the caller's own item type and `Multiple` turns it into an array, so no JSON Schema type can state it.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the initially chosen item, or an array of them with `multiple`, or null
defaultValue.because: Same generic type as `value`; the caller chooses `Value`, so no schema can state it.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a callback called with the next value and event details, not a value
onValueChange.because: `(value, eventDetails) => void`; the value is null in single mode when the choice is cleared, and the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (such as an item press, a clear press or a chip removal). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

inputValue.states: inputValue is the text in the field, controlled by the caller
inputValue.because: `string | number | readonly string[]`, the type of an input's `value` attribute - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

defaultInputValue.states: defaultInputValue is the text the field starts with
defaultInputValue.because: `string | number | readonly string[]`, the type of an input's `defaultValue` attribute - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

onInputValueChange.states: onInputValueChange is a callback called with the field's next text and event details, not a value
onInputValueChange.because: `(inputValue: string, eventDetails) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (such as a trigger press, an outside press or Escape). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the open or close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

onItemHighlighted.states: onItemHighlighted is a callback called with the highlighted item, or undefined, and details whose reason is keyboard, pointer or none
onItemHighlighted.because: `(highlightedValue: Value | undefined, eventDetails) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

items.states: items is the full list to filter, either a flat array of item values or an array of groups each holding its own `items` array
items.because: `readonly any[] | readonly Group<any>[]` - the schema asserts an array; what its entries are is the caller's own type.

filteredItems.states: filteredItems is a list filtered by the caller, shown instead of the root's own filtering of `items`
filteredItems.because: `readonly any[] | readonly Group<any>[]` - the schema asserts an array; what its entries are is the caller's own type.

filter.states: filter is a function deciding whether an item matches the typed query, or null to show every item unfiltered
filter.because: `((itemValue, query, itemToString?) => boolean) | null` - a function or null, which no JSON Schema type covers.

itemToStringLabel.states: itemToStringLabel is a function turning an object item into the text shown in the field and matched by the filter
itemToStringLabel.because: `(itemValue: Value) => string` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers. Items shaped `{ value, label }` need none; their label is used.

itemToStringValue.states: itemToStringValue is a function turning an object item into the string submitted with a form
itemToStringValue.because: `(itemValue: Value) => string` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers. Items shaped `{ value, label }` need none; their value is used.

isItemEqualToValue.states: isItemEqualToValue is a function deciding whether an item equals the chosen value, for object items that are not the same reference
isItemEqualToValue.because: `(itemValue: Value, value: Value) => boolean` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers; without it items are compared with `Object.is`.

multiple.states: multiple is a boolean that also switches the type of `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` to arrays
multiple.because: Typed as the root's `Multiple` type parameter; the schema asserts a boolean, and what it does to the other props' types is checked by tsc.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the root fills with an imperative `unmount` action
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<Actions | null>` - a ref object holding a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

inputRef.states: inputRef is a ref to the hidden native input Base UI renders for form submission
inputRef.because: `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - neither is expressible in JSON Schema.

locale.states: locale is the locale, or list of locales, the default filter compares strings in
locale.because: `Intl.LocalesArgument` - a string, a locale object or an array of them; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

good.title: One value from a filterable list
good.code:
<Combobox items={regions}>
  <ComboboxInput aria-label="Region" placeholder="Pick a region" showClear />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No regions found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
          {item}
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>

good.title: A value the caller owns
good.code:
<Combobox items={regions} value={region} onValueChange={setRegion}>
  <ComboboxInput aria-label="Region" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>

bad.title: Props from another library's autocomplete
bad.why: The root takes no `options` or `onChange`; the list goes in `items` and the chosen value is reported through `onValueChange`.

companions.description: Returns a ref for a multiple-value combobox: pass it to ComboboxChips as `ref` and to ComboboxContent as `anchor`, so the popup is placed against, and as wide as, the whole chips field rather than the inline ComboboxChipsInput inside it. A plain `useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)` does the same.
